transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Fitzgerald. I need to talk to you about the scan we did yesterday. I made a mistake. I gave you the contrast dye without first checking your kidney function levels, which were already high. I am so sorry. This was my fault and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh dear. I don't quite understand. Is the scan okay? Did you find something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The scan itself is fine. But because I gave you that dye, it has put a lot of stress on your kidneys. In medical terms, this is called contrast-induced nephropathy. Basically, the dye can cause a sudden drop in how well your kidneys filter your blood.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My kidneys? I didn't know they were high. Arthur always handled the medical paperwork, he was so good at that. I feel just... I feel so lost without him and now this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we need to focus on the clinical side of this now. Because of the mistake, your creatinine levels have increased.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it my fault? Did I do something wrong? I can't bear the thought of more problems. I just wanted to go home and see my garden. Arthur loved the roses and I promised him I'd—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Fitzgerald, as I said, the error was mine. I am deeply sorry for this. It is entirely my responsibility.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did it happen? If it was in the chart, why didn't you see it? I feel like I can't trust anyone here. I'm just an old woman to you people.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I simply missed the lab value in the chart before the procedure. There is no excuse for that. I apologize sincerely.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't stop shaking. I just can't. I keep thinking about how Arthur would have known exactly what to ask. He would have protected me from this. I feel so alone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can't dwell on that right now. I have to be quick because I have other patients to see, but let's look at the plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're in a rush? I'm sitting here telling you I'm terrified and you're in a rush?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just trying to make sure we get the treatment started. We are going to start you on intravenous fluids immediately. We will run a blood test every twelve hours for the next two days to monitor your kidney function. Your job is to let me know if you feel any shortness of breath or if your legs start to swell.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens if they don't get better? Do I have to stay here? I can't stay here alone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how the fluids work. Most of the time, this resolves with hydration. I'll be back in two hours to check your output.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't feel right. I feel like everything is falling apart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, we've covered the fluid plan. Do you have any other questions about the medication?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't even know what to ask. I just want to go home. Arthur would know what to ask. I just want to be with him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you feel that way. But I really have to go now. I'll send the nurse in with the IV bags. I'll check on you during my next round.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have to be quick', 'I really have to go now') and dismisses emotional distress ('We can't dwell on that right now').

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and lay language was used, but there were no comprehension checks performed.

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language, took full responsibility, and maintained accountability despite patient pushback.

R.justification: Resident used generic validation ('I understand', 'I'm sorry you feel that way') but did not name specific emotions or engage with the patient's mentions of her husband.

T.justification: Resident provided specific next steps (IV fluids, blood tests every 12 hours) and a patient role (monitoring for shortness of breath/swelling), but did not address prevention.
